item.title: Swedish word of the day: norrsken
item.description: The Northern Lights season has begun, but how do you talk about the phenomenon in Swedish?

item.title: How to take the best pictures of the Northern Lights
item.description: The Northern Lights season is here. Taking these pictures is an art itself and requires preparation, so The Local spoke to an expert to find out how to take awe-inspiring snaps of the natural phenomenon.

item.title: Which new laws affecting foreigners in Sweden will be published this spring?
item.description: Sweden's government has published its list of bills scheduled for spring. Tighter citizenship rules, ending issuance of permanent residency, and better rules for researchers are all in there. Revoking existing permanent residency permits is not.

item.title: OPINION: This is a 1938 moment for Europe, but the war will be a trade war
item.description: European leaders sending their troops to Greenland has - writes political columnist John Lichfield - called Donald Trump's bluff when it comes to military conflict. Instead the continent faces the prospect of a long and brutal trade war.

item.title: Why do men in Sweden vote for the right and women for the left?
item.description: Sweden’s left-wing parties would govern with a large majority if only women were allowed to vote. But if men had their way, the right would dominate completely. Why do women and men in Sweden view politics so differently and has the gap always been so wide?

item.title: Grammar guide: When to use compound words in Swedish
item.description: Särskrivning, or writing compound words in Swedish incorrectly as two separate words, is a common mistake among Swedish learners (and among Swedes in general, for that matter). But how do you avoid them?

item.title: What were Sweden's most popular baby names in 2025?
item.description: Vera leaped from fifth place to become the most popular name for baby girls in Sweden in 2025, while Noah was the most popular boy's name for the third year running, according to new statistics from the Swedish Tax Agency.

item.title: Swedish pensioners on how abolishing the wealth tax changed their country
item.description: In an article first published by The Conversation, UCL Senior Research Fellow in Social Anthropology Miranda Sheild Johansson speaks to a number of Swedish pensioners in southern Stockholm to learn how they feel about Sweden's decreasing levels of taxation.

item.title: Americans in Sweden: Are the Swedish treating you differently as international tensions rise?
item.description: Relations between the US and Europe - including Sweden - are increasingly tense and Swedish troops are now in Greenland after Donald Trump's threats to annexe the Danish territory - but are world events affecting the everyday lives of Americans in Sweden?

item.title: Today in Sweden: A roundup of the latest news on Wednesday
item.description: Greenland crisis could cause Swedish 'stagflation', new wolf territory in Östergötland, Social Democrats propose new law after Rönninge murder and more news from Sweden on Wednesday.
